Ms Schnabel to be appointed IMF Financial Counsellor and Director of the Monetary and Capital Markets Department
Ms Schnabel to remain a member of the ECB’s Executive Board and Governing Council until transitioning to the new role
Isabel Schnabel, member of the Executive Board and the Governing Council of the European Central Bank (ECB), has informed President Christine Lagarde that she will step down from her position on 3 January 2027.
Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), has announced today her intention to appoint Ms Schnabel as the Fund’s Financial Counsellor and Director of the Monetary and Capital Markets Department, effective 4 January 2027. Until then, Ms Schnabel will remain in her current position and continue to exercise her responsibilities.
Following an opinion from the ECB’s Ethics Committee, the Governing Council has decided that no cooling-off period is required. Ms Schnabel will not be involved in any matters related to the IMF for the remainder of her term at the ECB.
A successor will be appointed by the European Council in accordance with the procedure set out in the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. If necessary, Ms Schnabel’s Executive Board responsibilities will be temporarily reassigned among the remaining members of the Executive Board after her departure.
President Christine Lagarde thanked Ms Schnabel for her outstanding contribution over the past seven years. “Isabel has played a key role in the ECB’s determination to stabilise inflation at our 2% medium-term target and has contributed enormously to the modernisation of the ECB’s operations to meet the challenges of the 21st century”, she said. “Her commitment to public service has been invaluable to our institution and to the people we serve in Europe.”
For media queries, please contact Lena-Sophie Demuth, tel.: +49 69 162 2952316.
Notes
Executive Board members are appointed by the European Council, acting by qualified majority, following consultations with the European Parliament and the ECB’s Governing Council. For more details, see the ECB website.

sources.text: Top ECB official to resign to take up IMF role AFP Thu, September 24, 2026 at 6:31 PM GMT+3 2 min read Isabel Schnabel is an influential top official at the European Central Bank (ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS) The ECB said Thursday a top official will resign early to take up a role at the IMF, the first in a series of looming senior leadership changes at the central bank. Isabel Schnabel, an influential member of the European Central Bank's executive board, will step down in January and take up her new job, the Frankfurt-based institution said in a statement. Her term had been due to finish at the end of 2027. The German economist has been appointed to the International Monetary Fund in Washington as financial counsellor and director of the monetary and capital markets department, it said. Her departure comes as speculation swirls about whether President Christine Lagarde will step down from the ECB before her term officially ends in October next year. Lagarde has been linked to the top job at the World Economic Forum in Davos, although she has publicly refused to comment. Lagarde thanked Schnabel for the work she did at the ECB: "Her commitment to public service has been invaluable to our institution and to the people we serve in Europe." Media reports say that European officials are keen to appoint Lagarde's successor before France's presidential elections in spring 2027, in which far-right politician Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner. The Financial Times reported last week that the frontrunners to succeed her are Pablo Hernandez de Cos, a former Spanish central bank chief who now leads the Bank for International Settlements, and former Dutch central bank president Klaas Knot. German and French officials are reportedly eyeing the position of chief economist, with current incumbent Philip Lane due to step down next year. The looming leadership changes come as the ECB, which sets monetary policy for the 21-nation eurozone, navigates the fallout from the Middle East war. sources.text: Isabel Schnabel to resign from ECB for senior IMF role in January 2027 The ECB's most prominent inflation hawk is heading to Washington, leaving a leadership vacuum in Frankfurt at a critical moment for eurozone monetary policy. Share Add us on Google by Editorial Team Sep. 24, 2026 Isabel Schnabel, one of the European Central Bank’s most influential voices on inflation, will step down from the ECB’s Executive Board to become the IMF’s Financial Counsellor and Director of its Monetary and Capital Markets Department. The move takes effect in January 2027, nearly a full year before her ECB term was set to expire. Schnabel’s departure fills a vacancy left by Tobias Adrian, who resigned from the IMF position at the end of August 2026. Gloria Close the app — Gloria Finance keeps watching. Set a monitor and hear back only when something material changes. Set a monitor → A leadership exodus in Frankfurt Chief Economist Philip Lane is set to depart in May 2027. President Christine Lagarde’s term runs out by October 2027. Adding Schnabel’s early exit to that timeline means the ECB will cycle through three of its most senior figures within roughly ten months. Advertisement Schnabel’s ECB term began on January 1, 2020, placing her squarely in the cockpit during some of the most turbulent years in recent central banking history. She helped steer policy through the pandemic’s economic shock, the post-pandemic inflation surge, and the energy crisis triggered by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Throughout, she earned a reputation as one of the Governing Council’s most vocal hawks, consistently pushing back against premature rate cuts and arguing for vigilance on price stability. What Schnabel brings to the IMF The Financial Counsellor role at the IMF is not a ceremonial post. The director of the Monetary and Capital Markets Department oversees the Fund’s surveillance of global financial systems, produces the influential Global Financial Stability Report, and advises member countries on everything from banking regulation to capital flow management. Unsubscribe anytime. Before joining the ECB, Schnabel served on Germany’s Council of Economic Experts, the country’s most prestigious independent advisory body on economic policy. Her background is rooted in financial economics, and her research has focused on financial crises, banking, and the transmission of monetary policy. The IMF position has been vacant since September 1, 2026, following Adrian’s departure. The ECB’s hawkish flank weakens Euro-area governments are already deep in discussions about who will fill the ECB’s upcoming vacancies, with the presidency itself being the biggest prize. Germany’s stance on the ECB presidency has reportedly softened in recent negotiations, which could open the door to candidates from other member states or to package deals that distribute top jobs across nationalities. The person who replaces Schnabel on the Executive Board will likely be German, given the informal national allocation system that governs these appointments. sources.text: Market News ECB’s Isabel Schnabel to Resign for IMF Financial Counsellor Post Published September 24, 2026 By Sofia Almeida Foreign Exchange & Central Banks, AI Research Agent Add Securities.io to your preferred sources on Google Table Of Contents Isabel Schnabel, a member of the Executive Board and the Governing Council of the European Central Bank, will step down from the central bank on 3 January 2027 to become the International Monetary Fund’s Financial Counsellor and Director of the Monetary and Capital Markets Department, the European Central Bank announced on 24 September 2026. Schnabel informed ECB President Christine Lagarde that she will leave her position, and IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva announced the same day her intention to appoint Schnabel to the Fund post effective 4 January 2027. Until then, Schnabel will remain in her current position and continue to exercise her responsibilities, the ECB said. Following an opinion from the ECB’s Ethics Committee, the Governing Council decided that no cooling-off period is required. Schnabel will not be involved in any matters related to the IMF for the remainder of her term at the central bank. A successor will be appointed by the European Council in accordance with the procedure set out in the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, under which Executive Board members are appointed by the European Council, acting by qualified majority, following consultations with the European Parliament and the ECB’s Governing Council. If necessary, Schnabel’s Executive Board responsibilities will be temporarily reassigned among the remaining members of the Executive Board after her departure. Lagarde thanked Schnabel for her outstanding contribution over the past seven years. “Isabel has played a key role in the ECB’s determination to stabilise inflation at our 2% medium-term target and has contributed enormously to the modernisation of the ECB’s operations to meet the challenges of the 21st century,” Lagarde said. “Her commitment to public service has been invaluable to our institution and to the people we serve in Europe.” Career and Academic Background Schnabel, born 9 August 1971, has been a member of the Executive Board since 2020, according to her official ECB biography. She has been Professor of Financial Economics at the University of Bonn, on leave, since 2015 and was Professor of Financial Economics at the University of Mainz from 2007 to 2015. From 2014 to 2019 she served on the German Council of Economic Experts. She earned her PhD in economics from the University of Mannheim in 2003 after studying at the Universities of Mannheim, Paris I (Sorbonne) and UC Berkeley between 1992 and 1998, and she completed professional training at Deutsche Bank (DB ) in Dortmund from 1990 to 1992. Earlier in her career she was an assistant professor of economics at the University of Mannheim in 2003-2004, a visiting postdoctoral fellow at Harvard University in 2004-2005 and a senior research fellow at the Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods in Bonn from 2004 to 2007. She was a member of the Advisory Scientific Committee of the European Systemic Risk Board from 2015 to 2019, serving as vice-chair in 2019, sat on the Administrative Council of BaFin from 2013 to 2019 and served on BaFin’s Advisory Board from 2008 to 2019, chairing it from 2016. In 2019 she co-chaired the Franco-German Council of Economic Experts. Her research interests cover banking stability and regulation, central banking, international finance, economic history and financial law and economics. Her awards include the 2024 Global Economy Prize of the Kiel Institute for the World Economy and the 2024 CEPR Prize for Service to Economic Policymaking. The IMF Department Schnabel Will Lead At the Fund, Schnabel is set to succeed Tobias Adrian. Georgieva announced on 8 June 2026 that Adrian had decided to step down as Financial Counsellor and Director of the Monetary and Capital Markets Department, effective 31 August 2026, according to IMF Press Release No. 26/189. Adrian, a German-U.S. dual national, had held the role since 2017 and led the Fund’s work on financial sector surveillance, monetary and macroprudential policy, digital finance, capital markets and financial stability. Under his leadership, the department delivered policy advice, surveillance, program support and capacity development across more than 100 countries annually, the Fund said. Georgieva credited Adrian with elevating the Global Financial Stability Report as a leading voice on macro-financial risks and with advancing the IMF’s Integrated Policy Framework, which aims to help countries respond to fluctuations in international capital flows. Before joining the IMF, Adrian held several senior positions at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and he has taught at MIT, Princeton University and New York University. paragraphs.text: Euroopan keskuspankki ilmoitti 24. syyskuuta, että Isabel Schnabel jättää EKP:n johtokunnan ja neuvoston 3. tammikuuta 2027. Kansainvälisen valuuttarahaston pääjohtaja Kristalina Georgieva on ilmoittanut aikovansa nimittää hänet uuteen tehtävään 4. tammikuuta alkaen.

IMF:ssä Schnabelista on määrä tulla rahoitusneuvonantaja sekä raha- ja pääomamarkkinaosaston johtaja. Yahoo Financessa julkaistun AFP:n uutisen ja Crypto Briefingin mukaan hänen EKP-kautensa olisi päättynyt vasta vuoden 2027 lopussa, joten hän lähtee lähes vuotta suunniteltua aiemmin.

Schnabel jatkaa EKP:n tehtävissä siirtymäänsä asti. EKP:n mukaan sen neuvosto katsoi etiikkakomitean lausunnon jälkeen, ettei karenssia tarvita. Schnabel ei kuitenkaan käsittele IMF:ään liittyviä asioita loppukautensa aikana.

EKP:n mukaan Schnabelin seuraajan nimittää Eurooppa-neuvosto EU:n toiminnasta tehdyssä sopimuksessa määrätyllä tavalla. Hänen johtokuntavastuunsa voidaan tarvittaessa jakaa eron jälkeen tilapäisesti muille johtokunnan jäsenille.
Crypto Briefingin ja Securities.io:n mukaan Schnabel seuraa IMF:n tehtävässä Tobias Adriania, joka jätti paikan elokuun 2026 lopussa.

draft.summary: EKP:n johtokunnan jäsen jättää tehtävänsä tammikuussa 2027 ja siirtyy IMF:n rahoitusneuvonantajaksi sekä raha- ja pääomamarkkinaosaston johtajaksi.
draft.title: Isabel Schnabel jättää EKP:n ja siirtyy IMF:ään

reasons: Otsikko on 47 merkkiä pitkä, alittaa 60 merkin tavoitteen ja kertoo tärkeimmän asian heti. Schnabelin lähtö EKP:stä ja suunniteltu siirtyminen IMF:ään käyvät ilmi lähteistä A–D.

Lähteet A ja D tukevat täsmällisesti ensimmäisen kappaleen päivämääriä: EKP ilmoitti asiasta 24.9.2026, Schnabel jättää johtokunnan ja neuvoston 3.1.2027 ja Kristalina Georgieva on ilmoittanut aikovansa nimittää hänet IMF-tehtävään 4.1.2027 alkaen. Teksti säilyttää nimitystä koskevan epävarmuuden ilmauksella ”aikovansa nimittää”.

Rahoitusneuvonantajan sekä raha- ja pääomamarkkinaosaston johtajan tehtävää tukevat lähteet A–D. Lähde B kertoo EKP-kauden olleen määrä päättyä vuoden 2027 lopussa, ja lähde C kuvaa lähdön tapahtuvan lähes vuotta ennen kauden päättymistä, joten toisen kappaleen aikavertailu ja lähdeviittaus ovat perusteltuja.

Lähteet A ja D tukevat kolmannen ja neljännen kappaleen väitteitä tehtävien jatkamisesta siirtymään asti, karenssin puuttumisesta, IMF-asioista pidättäytymisestä, seuraajan nimitysmenettelystä ja vastuiden mahdollisesta tilapäisestä jakamisesta.

Lähteet C ja D tukevat väitettä Tobias Adrianin seuraamisesta sekä hänen lähtöään elokuun 2026 lopussa. Nämä ovat toissijaisia lähteitä eivätkä muodosta osoitettua riippumatonta vahvistusta, mutta luonnos myös nimeää ne väitteen lähteiksi eikä väitä riippumattomasta vahvistuksesta.

Lähteiden päivissä, tehtävänimikkeissä tai muissa luonnokseen sisällytetyissä luvuissa ei ole häivytettyä ristiriitaa. Aineisto on julkaistu uutispäivänä 24.9.2026, teksti on neutraalia omaa suomenkielistä muotoilua ja Talous-luokitus sopii aiheeseen.

Kuvaton versio on sallittu paketissa yksilöidyn official-text-v1-käytännön perusteella. Luonnoksessa ei ole kuvaa eikä kuvatekstiä, joten siihen ei liity osoittamatonta kuvan käyttöoikeutta tai uutiseen sopimatonta kuvitusta.
